1.why: src/testing/turns.ts is a frozen test helper of tasks 1 and 2 (Segment builder, seam-sequence generator, fold of Turn events); it imports types only, so each task's tests fail on their own missing module. Knowable end times follow the ticket's first Assumption: the finalizedAt of the Segment that proves the decision, or the last finalizedAt at the end of the Input.
1.addendum-2026-10-30: Gate-1 addendum (review of task 1). turn-builder.addendum.test.ts: the Segments each Turn event carries (turn-opened none, segment-appended up to and including the Segment, turn-ended all; never changed by a later push) and max_length after an interjection (181 s ends A's Turn, both ends known at 181 from push 3; exactly 180 s stays one Turn). turn-builder.held-cap.test.ts (owner decision 1): new optional builder parameter maxHeldSegments (default 200, integer >= 1, invalid values throw at createTurnBuilder naming maxHeldSegments); the Segment with which a held run would exceed it ends the ongoing Turn with speaker_change at its finalizedAt and the run opens the next Turn; bound per push P + 2 + (K+1)(K+2)/2 + 2(K+1) Segment references; fast-check seed 280306; the hostile generator stays under 2 s up to 512 Segments. The implementer adds the parameter without breaking START_VALUES (optional field) and updates the head comment of turn-builder.ts and the README 'Turns' paragraph.

2.interface: src/turns/tick-plan.ts: Tick { turn: Turn; time; upto; final }, createTickPlan(parameters) -> { next(event: TurnEvent): readonly Tick[] }. src/turns/tick-scheduler.ts: ExtractorName ('claim_extractor' | 'topic_extractor'), ExtractorCall { turn, segments (not yet sent, in order), final, at }, Extractor { call(call): Promise<{ latencySeconds }> } (the port T4 and T6 implement), createTickScheduler({ sessionId, extractors, logger }) -> { tick(tick): Promise<void>; drain(): Promise<void>; readonly skippedTicks }. Simulated clock: a call returns at at + latencySeconds; a return at exactly a Tick's time counts as returned. Full text in the headers of tick-plan.test.ts and tick-scheduler.test.ts.
implementerPaths: packages/service-kit/src/logger.ts and .claude/rules/platform.md (log fields for tick.skipped: the Turn id and the extractor; see owner question 1). The Logger type: task/27-3 (T2) already exports `type Logger` from @lfc/service-kit, so this lapses after the T2 merge
2.why: AC14 is tested as written: a non-final Tick without a new Segment is never counted, also while a call is in flight (the harness checks busy first; with Ticks from the Tick plan the case cannot occur, so parity is unaffected).
2.addendum-2026-10-30: Gate-1 addendum (review of task 2). tick-plan.addendum.test.ts: speech landing exactly on 5 s and going on (P2). tick-scheduler.addendum.test.ts: a Tick without a new Segment (AC14) during a call leaves that call in flight (S7, also with controllable promises and tick() not awaited); an interjection with tickSeconds 1 < interjectionMaxSeconds 2 gets its own non-final Tick and final analysis, its speech counts for no other Turn (P12, F1); a non-final Tick of a held-back run falls due at the release time, 15, for an interjection and for a run released by a third Speaker (F2; the Tick plan sees only next(event), so the release time has to reach it within the frozen interface). tick-scheduler.rethrow.test.ts (owner decision 3): a rejecting or throwing extractor call lets every call of the Tick settle, is logged as extractor.failed (three fields, no error text), then tick() rejects with the first original error object, first in ExtractorName order (F6); a final analysis waiting for that call (AC12) still starts at its own time with every Segment not yet sent and its tick() resolves; drain() never rejects. With decision 3 the implementer removes or changes the contradicting cases of the implementer-owned tick-scheduler.errors.test.ts (lines 86, 97, 109, 121, 164) and the 'never thrown / never reject' sentences in tick-scheduler.ts (head comment, TickScheduler.tick doc), services/detection/README.md 'Ticks' and .claude/rules/pipeline.md; #29 catches tick() rejections.
